--- name: wiki-docs description: Project document-vault conventions. Obsidian-compatible markup kept for what the terms need (wikilinks, block anchors, word entries), plus the reading face of every document — plain words, answer first, details folded, cards per section, captioned minimal figures. Use whenever a deliverable is a document that belongs to a project's knowledge base. --- # Wiki Docs — project document vault conventions Every markdown/HTML document written as a project deliverable (report, review, design note, investigation record) belongs to the project's document vault: write it into the vault, keep its terms citable vault-wide, and keep it readable as a standalone paper. Two faces must both hold, and they are NOT the same thing: - **The term face** (词条) — the part this standard protects hardest. A word entry is a block-anchored definition the whole vault can cite by name; wikilinks, block anchors, first-use citation and abbreviation expansion all exist to serve it. Those requirements are kept in full. - **The reading face** — a person has to get the answer in ten seconds. Plain words, the answer first, the argument folded away behind one click, one card per part, figures that show rather than explain. This is the writing-style-v2 discipline (clauses ⑨⑩⑪⑫ below). The nebflow wiki graph view still indexes the vault, but the graph is no longer a product we build towards (author order 2026-11-05 12:09): graph-shape rules that served nothing but link density were dropped or downgraded in this batch, and nothing on the term face was touched. ## Mandatory clauses (checkable — a violation is a rework) The thirteen clauses below are author mandates (2026-10-21; ④ added 2026-10-29, term-citation batch; ⑤ added 2026-10-30, card-face batch; ⑥ added 2026-11-05, images-live-with-the-doc batch — re-cut the same day with binding points ⑤⑥, "figures do not show" batch; ⑦⑧ added 2026-11-05, typography-and-abbreviations batch — author rulings 11:09 and 11:11; ⑨⑩⑪ added 2026-11-05, writing-style-v2 batch — author order 12:09; ⑫ added 2026-11-05, cite-terms-only batch; ⑬ added 2026-11-05 21:24, figure-first batch), not style advice. All thirteen are machine-checkable by the validator in `scripts/check_wiki_docs.py` (Python 3 stdlib only, zero deps) — except clause ⑤'s fence existence, which stays convention-enforced (skill + dispatch briefs) until the validator grows its existence rule (design §7.4, still open), and ⑪'s figure *style* (colours, widths, text budget), which a validator cannot judge — only its caption requirement is machine-checked: 1. **Vault format, every document (Obsidian-compatible, kept for the terms)** — written inside the vault `/projects//.stand/docs/` (the project's REGISTRATION dir, next to its `project.json` — NOT the project workspace repo; author ruling 2026-11-03), with a frontmatter block (`type:` / `status:`), references as wikilinks, attachments under `attachments/`. The Obsidian-compatible part is not decoration: `[[wikilink]]` + `#heading` + `^block-id` is the *only* syntax the term registry and the citation resolution read — drop it and 词条 stops working. → check rule `obsidian-format`. 2. **Cite what you build on (断链即缺陷；连线密度只是建议)** — when document B builds on document A, B cites A at the point of use. Broken references (missing target, missing `#heading` anchor, missing `^block-id`, an unregistered term short form) are defects. An orphan document with zero outgoing and zero incoming links is NOT a defect any more (writing-style-v2 batch, author order 2026-11-05 12:09): that rule only ever served graph link-density, and the graph is no longer built. It is printed as an advisory instead. → check rules `broken-link` / `broken-anchor` / `broken-block`; `orphan-doc` is advisory. Also downgraded / removed in the same batch: the "A gains a See-also link back to B" reciprocity rule (gone), the "wire every new document to glossary **or index.md**" requirement (the glossary half survives — it is the term face; the index half is gone). 3. **Every concept: explained or cited at first occurrence** — at a term's first mention there must be an inline one-sentence definition (dash / colon / parenthesis form), or a `[[glossary#^block-id]]` citation to the document that already defines it (a registered-term short form `[[Name]]` that resolves into the glossary counts as the citation). Multiple documents must never invent their own definition of the same concept — the glossary is the single definition source. → check rules `concept-first-use` / `duplicate-definition`. 4. **Term registry hygiene (词条引用批)** — a term is an explicitly declared, block-anchored definition: every glossary block entry and every `^term-*` declaration block must yield a term name via the ` —`/`：` separator convention, and within one document a term name is declared at most once. Short-form citations `[[Name]]` resolve through the term registry (glossary hit wins over doc-intro hits); a short form that is neither a document nor a registered term is a broken link. → check rules `term-format` / `term-duplicate` (R4; the citation face is R2 `broken-link`). 5. **Card face — a fenced ```human block is one card (card-face batch 2026-10-30, re-cut 2026-11-05)** — the product renders every ```human fence as ONE bordered card (`.nf-human-card`) and folds everything outside the fences into a collapsed drawer (`.nf-human-details`). That is the whole card mechanism; there is no second one (see "Card face" below). The opening card carries four parts in plain words: **结论 → 关键数字 → 图 → 待你决定的事** (no English heading, no jargon: "Impression" and its Chinese equivalents are on the blocklist, clause ⑨). Inside it: the conclusion in ≤3 lines, 3-7 key numbers, and **the caption sentence of the key chart** — the chart LINE itself goes **inside the card** — only the card body is on the first screen, everything outside the fences is folded into a collapsed drawer (`![[assets//key-chart.png]]`, caption = the conclusion sentence, path **vault-relative with its directory**, never a bare file name). The renderer expands image embeds inside a closed ```human fence as of the card-image batch (2026-11-05): the fence is not code, it is the card body, and `utils.js _transformHumanFace` re-renders that body as markdown — so a figure written in the card is a real figure on the first screen, while a figure written outside the fence is folded away (clause ⑥ binding point ⑥, rule `fence-embed-vault-relative`). Agent jargon (spec pass counts, merge-queue speak, worktree, commit hashes, session/chain internals) stays OUT of the card — plain wording, or a registered-term short form `[[Name]]` for terms that must stay (hover gloss via the term registry). Content outside the fences is the machine face: full detail, code anchors, acceptance readouts — written as fully as ever, presented folded. One document uses as many cards as it has parts (clause ⑩). → no validator rule for fence existence — deferred with the design (§7.4 另议); enforced by this skill + dispatch briefs until then. 6. **Images live with the document (图随文档走, images-live-with-the-doc batch, author order 2026-11-05 09:24)** — an image a document shows is a real file INSIDE the same vault (`/attachments/` or `/assets/`, i.e. under `/projects//.stand/docs/`), referenced by a vault-relative path — `![[key-chart.png]]` or `![](assets/key-chart.png)`. Never an absolute path, a `~` home path, a `file://` URL, a `../` path that escapes the vault, or an http(s) image host / CDN. The referenced file must EXIST. Rationale: the vault travels (other machines, fresh clones, cleaned worktrees), the repo evidence tree / worktree / cache does not — a document whose figures live elsewhere is a page of dead references the moment it moves. Two more binding points were added by the "figures do not show" batch (author report 2026-11-05, sample `agent-panel-three-row__20261105_201500.md`) — both are **renderer certainties**, not preferences: a document that breaks them shows a "image failed to load" placeholder or a line of literal text, no matter how correct the file location is. 5. **The reference must be the path the renderer actually builds.** Write the path **including the batch sub-directory**: `![[assets/20261105_agent-panel-rows/after-states-dark.png]]`, never the bare file name `![[after-states-dark.png]]`. The renderer's `imageCandidates()` (`src/main/resources/web/js/viewers/markdown.js:965`) builds a FIXED candidate list — document directory, vault root, `/attachments/`, `/assets/`, `/attachments/`, `/assets/` — and **never recurses into sub-directories**. A bare name for a figure stored in `assets//x.png` misses all six. → check rule `bare-name-embed` (R17): the violation prints the path you should have written. 6. **Figure lines go INSIDE the ```human card, with a vault-relative path.** The card mechanism renders a closed fence body as markdown and folds everything **outside** the fences into a collapsed drawer — so a figure written outside the card is folded away (first screen shows none of it), while a figure written in the card body is on the first screen. As of the card-image batch (2026-11-05) `expandImageEmbeds()` expands embeds inside a closed ```human fence too (`same file`, `humanCardBodyLines()`): the fence is the card body, not code. The path in there must be **vault-relative with its directory** (`assets//x.png`, `attachments/x.png`): that form resolves through the renderer's vault-root slot from ANY document directory, while a bare name only resolves from four of the six slots. → check rule `fence-embed-vault-relative` (R18). Generic code fences (```js and friends) still keep `![[…]]` literal — code is code. → check rules `image-outside-vault` (R6), `bare-name-embed` (R17), `fence-embed-vault-relative` (R18); per-occurrence escape hatch is the inline marker `` (see "Images live with the document" below). 7. **Typography: paragraph indent + restrained colour (排版批, author ruling 2026-11-05 11:09)** — every body paragraph starts with `  ` (two HTML entities = a two-character first-line indent; plain spaces either collapse to nothing or turn the line into a code block), and colour — which Markdown cannot produce, only inline HTML can — is capped at **4 spots per document** (3 recommended), only on **key conclusions and risk/warnings**, using exactly three fixed semantic values. Emphasis in general means **bold**, never colour. → check rules `doc-indent` / `doc-color`; full table, positive and negative examples in "Document typography" below. 8. **Every abbreviation expanded at first use (缩写批, author ruling 2026-11-05 11:11)** — domain abbreviations (GCR / SCD / DPC / MC / NIEL…) and organisation abbreviations (ICRP / IAEA / CERN / NIST…) must carry their full name at the **document's first occurrence**, either inline (`full name（GCR）`, `GCR（full name）`) or through a term link (`[[GCR]]（full name）`). Units and universal technical marks are exempt through the allowlist **written into this file** (not hidden in the script). → check rule `abbrev-expansion`; see "Abbreviations" below. 9. **Plain words (平实语言, writing-style-v2 batch, author order 2026-11-05 12:09)** — write so the reader never has to decode a word twice. Blocked: abstract-noun wrappers and personified jargon (the list is the marker block in "Plain language" below — `人面子`, `印象`, `抓手`, `赋能`, `闭环` …). The test is mechanical: **if a plain verb + noun can say it, an abstract noun must not wrap it**. Say "先写结论，再写细节", not "采用结论先行的叙事结构". Abbreviations still get expanded (clause ⑧); the two rules are different: ⑧ is about tokens, ⑨ is about words that are already Chinese and still opaque. → check rule `plain-language` (file:line + the suggested replacement from the blocklist). 10. **Answer first, details folded (结构三层, same batch)** — every document has three layers, in this order: **① the overall conclusion** (one paragraph at the top — the answer, not the background); **② a conclusion sentence at the head of each section** (one bold line); **③ the argument itself, inside a collapsed block** (`
…`), so a reader who trusts layer ② never sees layer ③ unless they click. → check rules `doc-structure` (section head is not a bold one-line conclusion) and `detail-fold` (a section's open prose over 600 visible characters with no `
` block; threshold via `--fold-threshold`); templates in "Document skeleton" below. 11. **Figures show, captions speak (图简约 + 图注, same batch)** — a figure carries the shape of the data, not the explanation of it. Minimal style: one accent colour at most, grey ramp plus dash patterns for series, no grid, no in-figure paragraphs, legend labels ≤ one short line. Everything the figure cannot say in three words goes into the **caption** (`图 N …`, one sentence stating the conclusion) and the body text. Every figure has a caption; a caption over 120 characters is a body paragraph wearing a caption's clothes. → check rule `image-caption` (missing) and the advisory `image-caption-long`; parameters, positive example and the DOSTEL baseline in "Figures in a document" below. 12. **Cite terms only (只许引用词条, cite-terms-only batch 2026-11-05)** — a reference points at a **term**, never at a document, never at a bare file path. Author wording: 「以后我们就只允许引用词条，不允许引用文档」「不允许 引用文档和图片路径，文档就用词条，图片要么直接嵌入，要么就可以点击跳转」. Allowed forms: registered-term short form `[[词条名]]` / `[[词条名|显示名]]`; positional references `[[doc#^term-slug]]` / `[[doc#Heading]]`; image **directly embedded** (`![[a.png]]`, `![](…)`, ``); image **clickable** (`[说明](attachments/a.png)`, `[[attachments/a.png|说明]]`). Defects: a bare `.md` path in prose (`见 design/foo.md`), a markdown link to a document (`[x](foo.md)`, `[x](foo.md#sec)`), a no-anchor `[[X]]` that resolves to a document but not to a registered term, a plain-text image path (`attachments/a.png`, `../a.jpg`, `/abs/a.png`), and a no-anchor `[[Name]]` that resolves to neither a document nor a registered term. Inline code and fenced code are exempt (a documented syntax example is not a citation). An inline `` (same line or the line directly above, non-empty reason) exempts that line — it never fails the run, but it is always printed as a count, and so is a stale marker on a clean line. → check rules `doc-reference` (R13) / `bare-image-path` (R14) / `dangling-term` (R15). The cite-terms batch first took R7/R8/R9; it yielded those numbers to the typography rules (R7 `doc-color` / R8 `doc-indent` / R9 `abbrev-expansion`, landed earlier and already in force) and moved up to R13–R15 — the judgement logic is unchanged, only the numbers. 13. **Figures are the document; words annotate them (以图为主, author ruling 2026-11-05 21:24)** — a visual report is a **figure-led** document: the body IS the figures (Mermaid / data charts / screenshots) and prose exists only to annotate and conclude. Author wording: 「一定要以图为主……文字要尽量少， 只说关键内容，然后不得不补充的细节，就放在可点击展开的块里」. Four binding points: (a) **Figure order = narrative order** — a reader scrolling the figures gets the whole argument without reading a paragraph. (b) **Words carry conclusions, decisions and readouts only** — process, derivation and item-by-item enumerations do not sit in the body. (c) **Whatever detail must stay goes into a collapsed block**, in the one compliant form `
过程` + blank line + body + blank line + `
`; the summary is a short label with information in it (「过程」「取证读数」「复现步骤」), never a whole sentence. (d) **Exceptions are declared in the document**, never taken silently — a step-by-step derivation document states why it is unfigured / unfolded, with the marker `` (reason non-empty) or ``. Anti-patterns, spelled out because they are what this clause was written against: a wall of explanatory prose; a tutorial on "how to drive the tool that draws the chart"; evidence pasted line by line into the body; a caption that restates what the figure already says. → check rules `image-required` (R19: a document with no figure at all) and `stacked-detail` (R20: a run of item-by-item readout / step lines outside any `
`); the whole discipline and its thresholds are in "Figure first, words annotate" below. Run before delivering any document batch: ``` python3 ${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/check_wiki_docs.py --project --glossary glossary.md ``` - The validator has a regression fixture — `scripts/test_check_wiki_docs.py` (stdlib `unittest`, builds throwaway vaults, covers rules R1–R12 + R16 (the renumbered `detail-fold`), the cite-terms-only trio R13–R15 and the red→green exit codes, including the typography/abbreviation cases: not expanded ⇒ flags, expanded ⇒ passes, unit allowlisted ⇒ passes, inside a code fence ⇒ not scanned, colour over budget ⇒ flags, missing indent ⇒ flags; and the writing-style-v2 cases: blocked word ⇒ flags with a suggestion, blocked word inside inline code ⇒ silent, section without a bold conclusion ⇒ flags, open prose over the fold threshold ⇒ flags, folded prose ⇒ passes, image without a caption ⇒ flags, over-long caption ⇒ advisory only, orphan document ⇒ advisory only; and the two later batches: bare-name embed ⇒ flags **with the path to write**, in-vault sub-directory path ⇒ passes, embed inside a human fence ⇒ flags, embed outside it ⇒ passes; document with no figure ⇒ flags, declared `wiki-figure-exempt` ⇒ passes, 12+ un-folded detail lines ⇒ flags, the same lines inside `
` ⇒ passes). Run it in the same breath as any validator change: `cd scripts && python3 -m unittest test_check_wiki_docs -v`. - **Scope of clauses ⑦⑧⑨⑩⑪⑫ (stock transition).** R7–R12, R16 and the cite-terms trio R13–R15 are enforced as violations for **new-format documents**: a stage document whose filename time block is ≥ `20261105_111100`, or any document that declares `style:` in its frontmatter (opt-in), or any document at all under `--strict-style` (the full-vault remediation sweep). Older stock is reported as **advisory** — printed with file:line and counted, but outside the violation list and the exit code — because 400 existing documents cannot be re-laid-out in one batch. Touch a legacy document and it comes into scope: fix what you touch. Flags: `--style-since `, `--strict-style`, `--skip-style`, `--allowlist`, `--allowlist-extra`, `--plainwords`, `--plainwords-extra`, `--fold-threshold `, `--style-since-v2 ` (R10–R12 and R16 take effect from their own stamp — `20261105_130000`, this batch's delivery; the `style:` frontmatter opt-in belongs to R7–R9 and does not retro-apply). - **Scope of clauses ⑥ ⑤⑥ and ⑬ (same stock transition, own stamps).** R17 `bare-name-embed` / R18 `fence-embed-vault-relative` are hard from `--image-since`, default `20261105_130000` (same reasoning as v2: documents written before the rule existed cannot be judged by it, so they print as advisory); R19 `image-required` / R20 `stacked-detail` are hard from `--figure-since`, default `20261105_212400` (the figure-first ruling's own moment). All four go hard for every document under `--strict-style`. The readout line `图能不能显示（R17-R18 …）` always prints both tiers, so a stock hit is visible even when it does not fail the run. - The vault root defaults to `/projects//.stand/docs/` (`STAND_HOME` / `NEBFLOW_HOME` override the data root); `--project` defaults to `stand`. `--root ` still overrides explicitly — use it to validate a not-yet-migrated workspace `docs/` vault. - Deliverables must pass with zero NEW violations (exit 0). Pre-existing legacy violations in the vault are not a pass for this batch — fix what you touch. - `--graph out.json` (optional, no document-side requirement) exports the same data the wiki index builds — `{nodes, edges}` — for offline analysis or a one-off visualisation; each doc node embeds its paragraph index (`paragraphs`: edge-form anchor / line range / ≤280-char excerpt) and its declared terms (`terms`: name / aliases / source `glossary|doc` / rel / anchor / line range / ≤280-char definition — isomorphic with WikiIndex.scala, the `GET /api/wiki/term` + `nodeJson.terms[]` consumption face, which is the term face and stays); `--json` machine-reads the violation list; exit codes: 0 clean, 1 violations, 2 usage error. - Paragraph-level references use the two in-vault anchor forms (validated by the same broken-anchor/broken-block checks): `[[doc#^block-id]]` addresses ONE paragraph (the glossary-entry face — noun explanations), `[[doc#heading]]` addresses a section. No `§` syntax exists — that glyph is a hover-overlay marker only. - Syntax examples with literal double brackets must live inside fenced code blocks — a bare `[[...]]` in prose is parsed as a real link (same semantics as the engine's WikiIndex parser). ## Vault layout - Vault root: `/projects//.stand/docs/` — created at project creation (idempotent); fall back to the workspace `docs/` only for a not-yet-migrated project (read-side compatibility, never for new writes). - Attachments (images, exports, data files referenced by documents): `/attachments/`, or `/assets/` (the newer batch convention — both are in-vault and both are acceptable). Never scatter attachments next to documents or in ad-hoc folders, and never point at a file outside the vault: every asset referenced by a document lives inside the vault and is referenced by its vault-relative path (clause ⑥). - One document = one topic. The file name is the document identity; prefer short kebab-case names (`auth-flow-review.md`), because other documents cite the file name. - **Document naming — key information first, time last (author ruling 2026-11-04 18:12; this bullet is the only naming rule for produced docs).** What the document IS leads the file name; time is a tail attribute. Stage documents (one-off diagnostics / audits / review snapshots) are named `___[__].md`: `topic`, then `__`, then the second-precision local time block (`YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS`, `_` inside the block; a same-second clash appends `-` to the time block), then `__` only when the producing chain is real — never invented. Living documents stay date-less (`.md`, `__` tail only when attributed). `topic` = lowercase kebab (English / pinyin) or verbatim CJK, one phrase that says what the document is; a bland word alone (`report`, `doc`, `notes`) is not a topic, and documents of one series share one topic prefix. Scope = produced documents and evidence (vault knowledge docs, `reports-evidence/`, `evidence/`); code, tests, specs and configs are out of scope. Existing documents keep their names — no rename, no move, no retro-edit (the date-first form survives only on that existing stock). - **Sub-project vaults (#744-B, layout only)**: any `/docs/` directory inside the vault is its own level — a sub-project keeps the same vault convention one level down (`docs//docs/`), so its own glossary and its own term names do not collide with the parent's. Cross-level citations use the target level's path form (`[[/docs/topic.md]]`) and are counted as cross-level links, never silently broken. The graph view used to render a parent node drilling into a child graph; that rendering is no longer a requirement — the layout rule and the per-level validation stay, because a term registry needs one definition source **per level**. Validate every level independently: `python3 ${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/check_wiki_docs.py --project --include-subvaults` ## Document form (paper style) - The document title is the first `# H1` heading. It is the document's name to the reader and the label any index or listing shows. - Structure: the overall conclusion first (one paragraph), then one conclusion sentence per section with its argument folded underneath (clause ⑩), then the appendix. - Every new concept must be understandable at first mention: either define it inline in one or two sentences at the point of first use, or link the definition to the document/section that defines it (see references below). Never leave a term that only a companion document explains without the link. (This is mandatory clause ③ — the validator above enforces it.) - Concepts that recur across documents belong in a glossary document (`glossary.md` at the vault root): one block per concept, each block ending with a block id, e.g. ``` Retry storm — a feedback loop where failures trigger retries that multiply load and produce more failures. ^retry-storm ``` ## Images live with the document (图随文档走, clause ⑥) Author order 2026-11-05 09:24: *"对 visual report 做要求，就是文档相关的图片要 放文档里"*. The rule governs the PHYSICAL LOCATION of figures only — the explain-at-first-occurrence discipline (clause ③) stays exactly as it was. **Scope (surface split, do not mix):** this clause governs images inside VAULT DOCUMENTS (the `.stand/docs/` markdown/HTML knowledge base, rendered by the vault's own resolver). Chart embedding in delivery text / chat cards is a different surface with a different resolver — there `skills/core/SKILL.md` §2 (absolute `~/...` paths inside the served whitelist) still applies. One artifact can serve both: generate into the whitelist, then copy the figure into the vault and reference the copy relatively from the document. Four binding points, all machine-checked as `image-outside-vault`: 1. **The file lives in the vault.** Any image a document shows sits under `/projects//.stand/docs/` — by convention `/attachments/` or `/assets/`; generated figures are copied into the vault in the same batch that writes the document. 2. **The reference is vault-relative.** `![[key-chart.png]]`, `![](assets/key-chart.png)`, `![](../assets/key-chart.png)` (from a sub-directory) — or `` in HTML. NOT absolute paths, NOT `~` home paths, NOT `file://` URLs (an absolute path breaks the moment the data root moves, even when it happens to point inside today's vault). 3. **Never a volatile location.** No `reports-evidence/`, no worktree path (`.nebflow/worktrees//…`), no `/tmp`, no `~/.stand/uploads/`, no `~/.stand/evidence/` — these get cleaned, archived or moved, and the document then holds a dead reference. Copy the figure into the vault FIRST, then reference the copy. (Naming note: the same three rules apply to naming — the copy is named by the document-topic convention, not by the evidence folder it came from.) 4. **Offline first — no remote image hosts.** http(s) images, CDNs and remote icon/image services are violations; if the only source is remote, download one local copy into the vault, reference that copy, and name the origin in the caption or the surrounding text. 5. **The path must be the one the renderer builds (write the sub-directory).** Batch figures live in `/assets//`; the reference must say so: `![[assets/20261105_agent-panel-rows/after-states-dark.png]]`. The renderer (`web/js/viewers/markdown.js:965 imageCandidates()`) builds a **fixed** candidate list — document directory, vault root, `/attachments/`, `/assets/`, `/attachments/`, `/assets/` — and never recurses. A bare `![[after-states-dark.png]]` misses all six, and the page shows the "image failed to load" placeholder even though the file is sitting in the vault. → check rule `bare-name-embed` (R17); the violation message prints the exact path to write. Note the division of labour with R6: R6 asks "is the figure in the vault", R17 asks "can the renderer find it" — a document can pass R6 and still show a broken image, and that gap is exactly what R17 was added for. 6. **Figure lines go inside the human card, not outside it.** The card mechanism renders the fence body as markdown and folds everything outside the fences into a collapsed drawer; a figure written outside is folded away (first screen: none of it), a figure written inside is on the first screen. `expandImageEmbeds()` expands embeds inside a closed ```human fence as of the card-image batch (2026-11-05) — the fence is the card body, not code. Write the image line **inside the card** with a **vault-relative path that includes the directory** (`assets//x.png`). → check rule `fence-embed-vault-relative` (R18). Generic code fences keep `![[…]]` literal — that part is unchanged. The sample that started this batch (one defect left after the card-image batch, where it used to be two): ````markdown ```human 图： ![[after-states-dark.png]] ``` ```` Today it renders — but only as a bare-name lookup, which fails whenever the figure sits in a sub-directory. One fix: write the path including `assets//` (R17 outside a fence, R18 inside it). The card keeps the figure AND the caption sentence; moving the line below the closing fence would now hide it in the drawer instead of fixing it. Correct (compliant): ```markdown ![Layer-2 · chat 1440 · 差异 9,762px（0.75%）](assets/20261105_design-spec-layer2-chat-1440.png) ``` Wrong (the 2026-11-05 counter-example, sanitised): a design-spec document in the vault whose 24 screenshots were left in the repository evidence tree and referenced from outside it — ```markdown ![](../../reports-evidence/20261105_design-spec-value-convergence/shots-layer2-post/chat-1440-dark.png) ![[reports-evidence/20261105_design-spec-value-convergence/shots-layer2-post/chat-1440-dark.png]] ``` Both forms are `image-outside-vault`. The document travels with the vault; the screenshots die with the worktree — the reader gets four broken images where the evidence should be. This card template is the surviving discipline and stays mandatory. - `…` paired tags (same batch, revised to tag form at 16:16 to avoid markdown-syntax collision) mark user-visible content in chat-facing deliverables: the product shows ONLY tagged content by default — everything outside (reasoning, tool narration) is stripped until the user expands the badge, and the expanded view shows the raw full text with the tags verbatim; untagged legacy content renders fully as before. Write tagged content WeChat-style (short direct paragraphs, conclusion first); tone/length follow the user's communication-style profile (`~/.stand/User.md`), defaulting to concise direct Chinese. In vault documents the pipeline renders the tags transparently (content shown, tags invisible). Spec: design doc §11 (docs/design/20261030_human-readable-presentation.zh-CN.md). ```markdown # legacy heading kept for the record ## Human face (报告头, 2026-10-30 batch) ``` The section you are reading replaces that heading; documents written before 2026-11-05 keep their `Impression` heading and are not retro-edited. ## References (citations — the term face, not a graph quota) Use Obsidian wikilinks. They render as clickable references, they resolve into the term registry, and they are how a reader jumps from a claim to its source: Since the cite-terms-only batch (clause ⑫, 2026-11-05) a reference must point at a **term** — not at a document, not at a bare path: - `[[词条名]]` / `[[词条名|显示名]]` — cite a registered term by name (the only whole-target form that is still legal without an anchor). - `[[glossary#^retry-storm]]` — cite a concept definition block (preferred for concepts: the reader jumps to the exact definition and the target paragraph is highlighted). - `[[auth-flow-review#Token lifetime]]` — positional reference into a section. Positional references stay legal because they resolve to a *place*, not to a document identity. - `![[architecture.svg]]` — embed an attachment from `attachments/`. - Not citations any more (rules R13/R14): `[text](topic.md)` (a markdown link to a document), a document short form `[[some-doc]]`, a bare path in prose (`见 design/foo.md`) and a plain-text image path (`attachments/a.png`). Cite the term, embed the image, or link it. Citation discipline (what survived the graph cut, 2026-11-05): - **A source you build on is cited at the point of use.** That is all a citation owes the reader — the reader can reach the source. It does NOT owe the graph a link pair. - **A document with zero outgoing and zero incoming links** is printed as an advisory, not a defect: the link-density rule only ever served the graph, and a self-contained note is a perfectly good document. If the note does introduce terms, register them (clause ④) — that is the face that matters. - **Glossary or bust:** concepts that other documents will cite belong in the glossary, not in one document's body. (The old "or wire it to `index.md`" requirement is gone with the graph; an index is a convenience, not a quota.) - **A "See also" link back** from A to B is a nice courtesy — no longer required, and never retro-edited into existing documents. - Anchors must exist: `#heading` must match a heading in the target document; `^block-id` must match a block id. A reference that resolves to nothing is the document-level equivalent of a broken build. - Need to point at something that has no term yet? Declare the term (`^term-` block) and cite the name — do not fall back to a document link or a path. ## Concept-reference format (agent-authored reports) When the reader of a report will meet an unfamiliar term, write the first mention as a definition or a concept reference, not as bare jargon: - Inline: "…the retry budget (the maximum share of requests that may fail and retry before the circuit opens)…" - Reference: "…the retry budget ([[glossary#^retry-budget]])…" HTML deliverables follow the same discipline with plain anchors to the companion markdown documents in the vault. ## Terms and short-form citations (词条, term-citation batch 2026-10-29) A term is a named, block-anchored definition the whole vault can cite by name. Two declaration faces, both derived from the block-anchor paragraphs the term registry indexes — never declared in frontmatter (a `terms:` frontmatter list would be a second source of truth that drifts from the body anchors): - **Glossary terms** (cross-document shared concepts): every block-anchored entry of a glossary document (file whose name contains `glossary`) is a term. This is the single definition source (mandatory clause ③). - **Document-intro terms** (a document introducing its own topic, or its citable plans/attribution findings): declare them in a `## 词条` section near the top of the document. ONE entry per paragraph — a blank line between entries — each ending with a `^term-` block id: ``` ## 词条 - DCL（DOMContentLoaded 事件） — the browser's first interactive moment. #proj/stand #topic/term-index ^term-dcl - 归因结论 — this incident was caused by config drift, not code. #proj/stand #topic/incident ^term-attribution ``` Declaration shape (machine-checked, rule `term-format`): - The name is the text before the first ` —` (em/en dash) or `：`/`:` separator; no separator means the block is NOT a term and R4 flags it. - A trailing parenthetical group derives lookup aliases: `DCL（DOMContentLoaded 事件）` is citeable as `[[DCL]]`, `[[银河宇宙线]]`-style inner names likewise. Do not invent other alias syntaxes — the pipe is the wikilink reference alias (`[[target|display]]`), not a declaration face. - Within one document a term name is unique (rule `term-duplicate`). - The same term name MAY live in several documents' intro blocks (each document self-introduces) — but `[[Name]]` then stays unresolved: the engine never guesses between same-tier hits. ### Term tags (词条标签, term-system v2) Every term declaration carries a tag tail so the index can group terms by project and topic without a second source of truth. **One line, fixed order:** ``` - 词条名（别名1，别名2） — 一句话定义。 #proj/ #topic/ [更多 #topic/…] [更多 #/] ^term- ``` - **Exactly one** `#proj/` and **at least one** `#topic/`. Every other `#/` is an extra facet and is free-form (`#ctx/browser`, `#level/deep`, …). Facets are `facet/value` pairs — one slash; `#ctx/a/b` only registers `ctx/a`. - **Position**: the tags sit AFTER the definition text and BEFORE the `^term-` block id. The block id must be the last thing on its line. The tag window is exactly "after the ` —`/`：` separator → before the block id", so a tag written before the separator, or after the block id, is not read at all. - Tags are **decoration, never identity**: they add no aliases and change no citation resolution. `[[Name]]` still resolves by name/alias only. - `` `#x` `` inside an inline-code span is documentation, not a tag (write examples backticked); fenced code never enters a paragraph at all. - Buckets are deduplicated and sorted by the engine, so the same declaration always yields the same `{project, topic, extra}` JSON in every consumer. Valid (both buckets present, tags before the block id): ``` - DCL（DOMContentLoaded 事件） — 浏览器首次可交互的时间点。 #proj/stand #topic/term-index ^term-dcl - 归因结论 — 本批缺陷由配置漂移引入，不是代码回归。 #proj/stand #topic/incident #ctx/release ^term-attribution ``` **Invalid** — each one fails the check with the reason marked: ``` - GCR — 银河宇宙线通量。 #topic/cosmology ^gcr ``` ✗ **missing `#proj/`** — only a topic tag was written; a term with no project facet is unfilterable ⇒ `term-tag-missing`. ``` - 重试风暴 — 短时高频重试打满下游配额。 #proj/stand ^term-retry-storm ``` ✗ **missing `#topic/`** — the project tag never satisfies the topic requirement (`#topic/` is at least one, `#proj/` exactly one) ⇒ `term-tag-missing`. ``` - 举证窗口 — 规则允许补证的时长。 ^term-evidence-window #proj/stand #topic/compliance ``` ✗ **tags after the block id** — `^term-evidence-window` is no longer at line end, so Obsidian does not treat it as a block anchor, the paragraph is not a term, and the tags are invisible ⇒ `term-tag-missing`. Violation code `term-tag-missing` (R4): a term declaration whose tag set has no `#proj/` or no `#topic/` — including the "tags after the block id" form, which silently loses both. Fix the declaration line; the only escape hatch is an inline exemption `` on the same or the immediately preceding line with a non-empty reason (counted separately in the report, never a whole-file waiver). Citation resolution for `[[Name]]` (no anchor) — fixed priority: 1. exact vault-relative path → 2. unique basename document → 3. **term registry** (a unique glossary hit beats doc-intro hits) → 4. still ambiguous/unhit = unresolved (a dangling term in R15's report; a hit on step 1/2 with no term behind it is an R13 doc-reference). Practical discipline: cite `[[Name]]` when the name is unique vault-wide or glossary-defined; when you mean a SPECIFIC document's term (its plan, its attribution), cite `[[doc#^term-slug]]` explicitly. `[[Name|display]]` aliases ride the same resolution. Engine faces that consume the registry (no extra work for the writer): `GET /api/wiki/term?name=…&project=…` (single lookup: `{found, resolved, term}` / `{resolved:false, ambiguous, candidates}` / 404 unregistered), and each document node's `terms[]` projection (hover preview + deep links) — this is the term face's engine side, and it is untouched by the graph cut. Scope v1: term definitions are a markdown face — html documents get reference jumps with a document-level summary fallback, no html definition blocks. ## What not to do - Do not write reports outside the vault (chat-only delivery leaves the terms unciteable). - Do not bury the answer — the opening card (clause ⑤) states it, every section head states its own (clause ⑩); argument never precedes answers. - Do not write a section whose first line is a paragraph — one bold sentence first, argument folded underneath. - Do not explain inside a figure — the frame holds labels; the caption holds the conclusion; the body holds the reasoning. - Do not reach for an abstract noun when a verb is available (`对口径做一次 对齐` → `把两处数字改成一致`). - Do not duplicate a concept's definition in several documents — define once, reference everywhere else. - Do not use bare file paths as references; a link or a term citation is the reference, a plain path string is not. - Do not cite a **document**: no `[[some-doc]]` short form, no `[text](some-doc.md)`, no bare path in prose. Cite the term instead (clause ⑫, rules R13/R15). - Do not write an **image path as text**: no `attachments/a.png` in prose, no `../x.jpg`, no absolute path. Embed the image (`![[a.png]]`) or make it clickable (`[说明](attachments/a.png)`); rule R14. - Do not rename documents that are already cited; fix the citing links in the same change instead. ### Cite terms, not documents — the hard rule with examples The rule (author, 2026-11-05): 「以后我们就只允许引用词条，不允许引用文档」 「不允许引用文档和图片路径，文档就用词条，图片要么直接嵌入，要么就可以点击跳转」. Every line below is checked by R13/R14/R15; inline code and fenced code are the only places where a path-looking string is documentation rather than a citation. **OK — a term, a positional reference, an embed or a clickable image:** ``` 缓存击穿（cache stampede） — 同一热点键过期瞬间被并发打穿。 #proj/stand #topic/cache ^term-stampede 见 [[缓存击穿]]；实现细节见 [[缓存设计__20261105_101500#^term-stampede]]。 键表看 [[缓存设计__20261105_101500#Key table]]（整节定位）。 ![[stampede-chart.png]] 是这次事故的尖峰曲线。 [stampede-chart.png](attachments/stampede-chart.png) 可点击打开原图。 语法示例写在反引号里：`见 design/foo.md`。 ``` **Not OK — each line fails, with the reason:** ``` 见 design/foo.md。 → R13 doc-reference（正文裸 .md 路径） 细节见 [缓存设计](cache-design.md)。 → R13 doc-reference（markdown 链接指向文档） 参考 [[cache-design]]。 → R13 doc-reference（无锚短形解析到文档而非词条） 截图在 attachments/stampede-chart.png 里。 → R14 bare-image-path（图片路径是纯文本） 见 [[尚未注册的词条名]]。 → R15 dangling-term（文档与词条双双解析不到） ``` Fixing them: declare the term (`^term-`) and cite its name; point at a place with `[[doc#^term-slug]]` / `[[doc#Heading]]`; embed or link the image. While a legacy document is being migrated in another batch, put `` on the offending line (or the line directly above) — the run stays green, but the exemption is always printed as a counted line in the report, and a marker on a clean line shows up as a dangling annotation. There is no whole-file waiver. ## Frontmatter (scenario metadata) Every vault document starts with a tiny frontmatter block: ``` --- type: research-log status: open --- ``` - `type` names the document's role in the scenario pack (below); readers and tooling filter by it. - `status` says where the document stands. The statuses that mark finished work (`solved` / `done` / `accepted` / `mastered` / `published`) read as "already resolved" at a glance when a listing shows them. (The graph used to draw a ✓ ring on them; the field is unchanged and still worth filling — it is the only machine-readable progress signal a document carries.) ## Scenario packs Pick the pack that matches the engagement; do not invent a new one when these fit. ### Research (科研) A research engagement is a line of work, not a pile of files. Four document roles carry the line: - `research-log` (`status: open` while active): dated entries. Each entry links what it produced that day — experiments, notes, decisions — with wikilinks, so the log stays the reading order for the work. - `problem` documents: one open question each (`status: open`). When it is resolved, flip to `status: solved` and link the evidence (result document, experiment, literature note) at the resolution point. A solved problem that cites nothing is not closed. - `literature-note`: one per paper (title = paper short title). **Download the original PDF into `attachments/`** (use the `paper-download` skill of browser-use; filename convention `firstauthor-year-shorttitle.pdf`) and link it from the note — `![[firstauthor-year-shorttitle.pdf]]` — so the reader opens the original in canvas from the note. Remote-only links (URLs without a local copy) are a defect: literature research must produce the original file. Cite claims as `[[literature-note#^claim-id]]` block references. - `conclusion` documents: one settled finding each, citing the problem documents and literature notes that support it. Progress readout = the `status` fields: open problems, solved problems, conclusions. ### Learning (学习) - `learning-map`: the index document — one section per knowledge area, each knowledge point a wikilink to its own document. The map is the reading order. - Knowledge-point documents: one concept each; link prerequisite points (`Prerequisites: [[point-a]], [[point-b]]`) so a reader can walk the dependency order. - Study materials (course PDFs, slides, screenshots) go to `attachments/` and are cited from the point they belong to — same download-and-link discipline as research literature. - Progress = `status` on each point: `to-learn` / `learning` / `mastered`. ### Engineering (工程决策) - `adr` (architecture decision record): one decision each, `status: proposed | accepted | superseded`; a superseded ADR links its successor. Incident/postmortem documents cite the ADRs they constrain. - Experiment/verification records cite the ADR or problem that motivated them. ### Writing (写作) - `manuscript` (draft chapters), `source-note` (one per source, original downloaded to `attachments/` where licensable), `outline`. Sources cite claims with block references; the manuscript cites its sources. ### Team knowledge base (团队知识库) - `runbook` (operational procedures, kept current — stale runbooks get `status: superseded` with a link to the replacement), `faq` (one question per document), `onboarding` (index linking the reading path). ## Attachments are first-class references A wikilink or embed pointing at a canvas-openable attachment (PDF, Office, image, media) — `[[paper.pdf]]`, `![[figure.png]]` — opens it directly in canvas. Cite the attachment, never a bare path string: the link is what makes it reachable, and it also gives the term registry something to resolve against. The graph view listing attachments as nodes is a side effect, not a goal.

--- name: wiki-docs description: Project document-vault conventions. Obsidian-compatible markup kept for what the terms need (wikilinks, block anchors, word entries), plus the reading face of every document — plain words, answer first, details folded, cards per section, captioned minimal figures. Use whenever a deliverable is a document that belongs to a project's knowledge base. --- # Wiki Docs — project document vault conventions Every markdown/HTML document written as a project deliverable (report, review, design note, investigation record) belongs to the project's document vault: write it into the vault, keep its terms citable vault-wide, and keep it readable as a standalone paper. Two faces must both hold, and they are NOT the same thing: - **The term face** (词条) — the part this standard protects hardest. A word entry is a block-anchored definition the whole vault can cite by name; wikilinks, block anchors, first-use citation and abbreviation expansion all exist to serve it. Those requirements are kept in full. - **The reading face** — a person has to get the answer in ten seconds. Plain words, the answer first, the argument folded away behind one click, one card per part, figures that show rather than explain. This is the writing-style-v2 discipline (clauses ⑨⑩⑪⑫ below). The nebflow wiki graph view still indexes the vault, but the graph is no longer a product we build towards (author order 2026-11-05 12:09): graph-shape rules that served nothing but link density were dropped or downgraded in this batch, and nothing on the term face was touched. ## Mandatory clauses (checkable — a violation is a rework) The thirteen clauses below are author mandates (2026-10-21; ④ added 2026-10-29, term-citation batch; ⑤ added 2026-10-30, card-face batch; ⑥ added 2026-11-05, images-live-with-the-doc batch — re-cut the same day with binding points ⑤⑥, "figures do not show" batch; ⑦⑧ added 2026-11-05, typography-and-abbreviations batch — author rulings 11:09 and 11:11; ⑨⑩⑪ added 2026-11-05, writing-style-v2 batch — author order 12:09; ⑫ added 2026-11-05, cite-terms-only batch; ⑬ added 2026-11-05 21:24, figure-first batch), not style advice. All thirteen are machine-checkable by the validator in `scripts/check_wiki_docs.py` (Python 3 stdlib only, zero deps) — except clause ⑤'s fence existence, which stays convention-enforced (skill + dispatch briefs) until the validator grows its existence rule (design §7.4, still open), and ⑪'s figure *style* (colours, widths, text budget), which a validator cannot judge — only its caption requirement is machine-checked: 1. **Vault format, every document (Obsidian-compatible, kept for the terms)** — written inside the vault `/projects//.stand/docs/` (the project's REGISTRATION dir, next to its `project.json` — NOT the project workspace repo; author ruling 2026-11-03), with a frontmatter block (`type:` / `status:`), references as wikilinks, attachments under `attachments/`. The Obsidian-compatible part is not decoration: `[[wikilink]]` + `#heading` + `^block-id` is the *only* syntax the term registry and the citation resolution read — drop it and 词条 stops working. → check rule `obsidian-format`. 2. **Cite what you build on (断链即缺陷；连线密度只是建议)** — when document B builds on document A, B cites A at the point of use. Broken references (missing target, missing `#heading` anchor, missing `^block-id`, an unregistered term short form) are defects. An orphan document with zero outgoing and zero incoming links is NOT a defect any more (writing-style-v2 batch, author order 2026-11-05 12:09): that rule only ever served graph link-density, and the graph is no longer built. It is printed as an advisory instead. → check rules `broken-link` / `broken-anchor` / `broken-block`; `orphan-doc` is advisory. Also downgraded / removed in the same batch: the "A gains a See-also link back to B" reciprocity rule (gone), the "wire every new document to glossary **or index.md**" requirement (the glossary half survives — it is the term face; the index half is gone). 3. **Every concept: explained or cited at first occurrence** — at a term's first mention there must be an inline one-sentence definition (dash / colon / parenthesis form), or a `[[glossary#^block-id]]` citation to the document that already defines it (a registered-term short form `[[Name]]` that resolves into the glossary counts as the citation). Multiple documents must never invent their own definition of the same concept — the glossary is the single definition source. → check rules `concept-first-use` / `duplicate-definition`. 4. **Term registry hygiene (词条引用批)** — a term is an explicitly declared, block-anchored definition: every glossary block entry and every `^term-*` declaration block must yield a term name via the ` —`/`：` separator convention, and within one document a term name is declared at most once. Short-form citations `[[Name]]` resolve through the term registry (glossary hit wins over doc-intro hits); a short form that is neither a document nor a registered term is a broken link. → check rules `term-format` / `term-duplicate` (R4; the citation face is R2 `broken-link`). 5. **Card face — a fenced ```human block is one card (card-face batch 2026-10-30, re-cut 2026-11-05)** — the product renders every ```human fence as ONE bordered card (`.nf-human-card`) and folds everything outside the fences into a collapsed drawer (`.nf-human-details`). That is the whole card mechanism; there is no second one (see "Card face" below). The opening card carries four parts in plain words: **结论 → 关键数字 → 图 → 待你决定的事** (no English heading, no jargon: "Impression" and its Chinese equivalents are on the blocklist, clause ⑨). Inside it: the conclusion in ≤3 lines, 3-7 key numbers, and **the caption sentence of the key chart** — the chart LINE itself goes **inside the card** — only the card body is on the first screen, everything outside the fences is folded into a collapsed drawer (`![[assets//key-chart.png]]`, caption = the conclusion sentence, path **vault-relative with its directory**, never a bare file name). The renderer expands image embeds inside a closed ```human fence as of the card-image batch (2026-11-05): the fence is not code, it is the card body, and `utils.js _transformHumanFace` re-renders that body as markdown — so a figure written in the card is a real figure on the first screen, while a figure written outside the fence is folded away (clause ⑥ binding point ⑥, rule `fence-embed-vault-relative`). Agent jargon (spec pass counts, merge-queue speak, worktree, commit hashes, session/chain internals) stays OUT of the card — plain wording, or a registered-term short form `[[Name]]` for terms that must stay (hover gloss via the term registry). Content outside the fences is the machine face: full detail, code anchors, acceptance readouts — written as fully as ever, presented folded. One document uses as many cards as it has parts (clause ⑩). → no validator rule for fence existence — deferred with the design (§7.4 另议); enforced by this skill + dispatch briefs until then. 6. **Images live with the document (图随文档走, images-live-with-the-doc batch, author order 2026-11-05 09:24)** — an image a document shows is a real file INSIDE the same vault (`/attachments/` or `/assets/`, i.e. under `/projects//.stand/docs/`), referenced by a vault-relative path — `![[key-chart.png]]` or `![](assets/key-chart.png)`. Never an absolute path, a `~` home path, a `file://` URL, a `../` path that escapes the vault, or an http(s) image host / CDN. The referenced file must EXIST. Rationale: the vault travels (other machines, fresh clones, cleaned worktrees), the repo evidence tree / worktree / cache does not — a document whose figures live elsewhere is a page of dead references the moment it moves. Two more binding points were added by the "figures do not show" batch (author report 2026-11-05, sample `agent-panel-three-row__20261105_201500.md`) — both are **renderer certainties**, not preferences: a document that breaks them shows a "image failed to load" placeholder or a line of literal text, no matter how correct the file location is. 5. **The reference must be the path the renderer actually builds.** Write the path **including the batch sub-directory**: `![[assets/20261105_agent-panel-rows/after-states-dark.png]]`, never the bare file name `![[after-states-dark.png]]`. The renderer's `imageCandidates()` (`src/main/resources/web/js/viewers/markdown.js:965`) builds a FIXED candidate list — document directory, vault root, `/attachments/`, `/assets/`, `/attachments/`, `/assets/` — and **never recurses into sub-directories**. A bare name for a figure stored in `assets//x.png` misses all six. → check rule `bare-name-embed` (R17): the violation prints the path you should have written. 6. **Figure lines go INSIDE the ```human card, with a vault-relative path.** The card mechanism renders a closed fence body as markdown and folds everything **outside** the fences into a collapsed drawer — so a figure written outside the card is folded away (first screen shows none of it), while a figure written in the card body is on the first screen. As of the card-image batch (2026-11-05) `expandImageEmbeds()` expands embeds inside a closed ```human fence too (`same file`, `humanCardBodyLines()`): the fence is the card body, not code. The path in there must be **vault-relative with its directory** (`assets//x.png`, `attachments/x.png`): that form resolves through the renderer's vault-root slot from ANY document directory, while a bare name only resolves from four of the six slots. → check rule `fence-embed-vault-relative` (R18). Generic code fences (```js and friends) still keep `![[…]]` literal — code is code. → check rules `image-outside-vault` (R6), `bare-name-embed` (R17), `fence-embed-vault-relative` (R18); per-occurrence escape hatch is the inline marker `` (see "Images live with the document" below). 7. **Typography: paragraph indent + restrained colour (排版批, author ruling 2026-11-05 11:09)** — every body paragraph starts with `  ` (two HTML entities = a two-character first-line indent; plain spaces either collapse to nothing or turn the line into a code block), and colour — which Markdown cannot produce, only inline HTML can — is capped at **4 spots per document** (3 recommended), only on **key conclusions and risk/warnings**, using exactly three fixed semantic values. Emphasis in general means **bold**, never colour. → check rules `doc-indent` / `doc-color`; full table, positive and negative examples in "Document typography" below. 8. **Every abbreviation expanded at first use (缩写批, author ruling 2026-11-05 11:11)** — domain abbreviations (GCR / SCD / DPC / MC / NIEL…) and organisation abbreviations (ICRP / IAEA / CERN / NIST…) must carry their full name at the **document's first occurrence**, either inline (`full name（GCR）`, `GCR（full name）`) or through a term link (`[[GCR]]（full name）`). Units and universal technical marks are exempt through the allowlist **written into this file** (not hidden in the script). → check rule `abbrev-expansion`; see "Abbreviations" below. 9. **Plain words (平实语言, writing-style-v2 batch, author order 2026-11-05 12:09)** — write so the reader never has to decode a word twice. Blocked: abstract-noun wrappers and personified jargon (the list is the marker block in "Plain language" below — `人面子`, `印象`, `抓手`, `赋能`, `闭环` …). Embed the image (`![[a.png]]`) or make it clickable (`[说明](attachments/a.png)`); rule R14. - Do not rename documents that are already cited; fix the citing links in the same change instead. ### Cite terms, not documents — the hard rule with examples The rule (author, 2026-11-05): 「以后我们就只允许引用词条，不允许引用文档」 「不允许引用文档和图片路径，文档就用词条，图片要么直接嵌入，要么就可以点击跳转」. Every line below is checked by R13/R14/R15; inline code and fenced code are the only places where a path-looking string is documentation rather than a citation. **OK — a term, a positional reference, an embed or a clickable image:** ``` 缓存击穿（cache stampede） — 同一热点键过期瞬间被并发打穿。 #proj/stand #topic/cache ^term-stampede 见 [[缓存击穿]]；实现细节见 [[缓存设计__20261105_101500#^term-stampede]]。 键表看 [[缓存设计__20261105_101500#Key table]]（整节定位）。 ![[stampede-chart.png]] 是这次事故的尖峰曲线。 [stampede-chart.png](attachments/stampede-chart.png) 可点击打开原图。 语法示例写在反引号里：`见 design/foo.md`。 ``` **Not OK — each line fails, with the reason:** ``` 见 design/foo.md。 → R13 doc-reference（正文裸 .md 路径） 细节见 [缓存设计](cache-design.md)。 → R13 doc-reference（markdown 链接指向文档） 参考 [[cache-design]]。 → R13 doc-reference（无锚短形解析到文档而非词条） 截图在 attachments/stampede-chart.png 里。 → R14 bare-image-path（图片路径是纯文本） 见 [[尚未注册的词条名]]。 → R15 dangling-term（文档与词条双双解析不到） ``` Fixing them: declare the term (`^term-`) and cite its name; point at a place with `[[doc#^term-slug]]` / `[[doc#Heading]]`; embed or link the image. While a legacy document is being migrated in another batch, put `` on the offending line (or the line directly above) — the run stays green, but the exemption is always printed as a counted line in the report, and a marker on a clean line shows up as a dangling annotation. There is no whole-file waiver. ## Frontmatter (scenario metadata) Every vault document starts with a tiny frontmatter block: ``` --- type: research-log status: open --- ``` - `type` names the document's role in the scenario pack (below); readers and tooling filter by it. - `status` says where the document stands. The statuses that mark finished work (`solved` / `done` / `accepted` / `mastered` / `published`) read as "already resolved" at a glance when a listing shows them. (The graph used to draw a ✓ ring on them; the field is unchanged and still worth filling — it is the only machine-readable progress signal a document carries.) ## Scenario packs Pick the pack that matches the engagement; do not invent a new one when these fit. ### Research (科研) A research engagement is a line of work, not a pile of files. Four document roles carry the line: - `research-log` (`status: open` while active): dated entries. Each entry links what it produced that day — experiments, notes, decisions — with wikilinks, so the log stays the reading order for the work. - `problem` documents: one open question each (`status: open`). When it is resolved, flip to `status: solved` and link the evidence (result document, experiment, literature note) at the resolution point. A solved problem that cites nothing is not closed. - `literature-note`: one per paper (title = paper short title). **Download the original PDF into `attachments/`** (use the `paper-download` skill of browser-use; filename convention `firstauthor-year-shorttitle.pdf`) and link it from the note — `![[firstauthor-year-shorttitle.pdf]]` — so the reader opens the original in canvas from the note. Remote-only links (URLs without a local copy) are a defect: literature research must produce the original file. Cite claims as `[[literature-note#^claim-id]]` block references. - `conclusion` documents: one settled finding each, citing the problem documents and literature notes that support it. Progress readout = the `status` fields: open problems, solved problems, conclusions. ### Learning (学习) - `learning-map`: the index document — one section per knowledge area, each knowledge point a wikilink to its own document. The map is the reading order. - Knowledge-point documents: one concept each; link prerequisite points (`Prerequisites: [[point-a]], [[point-b]]`) so a reader can walk the dependency order. - Study materials (course PDFs, slides, screenshots) go to `attachments/` and are cited from the point they belong to — same download-and-link discipline as research literature. - Progress = `status` on each point: `to-learn` / `learning` / `mastered`. ### Engineering (工程决策) - `adr` (architecture decision record): one decision each, `status: proposed | accepted | superseded`; a superseded ADR links its successor. Incident/postmortem documents cite the ADRs they constrain. - Experiment/verification records cite the ADR or problem that motivated them. ### Writing (写作) - `manuscript` (draft chapters), `source-note` (one per source, original downloaded to `attachments/` where licensable), `outline`. Sources cite claims with block references; the manuscript cites its sources. ### Team knowledge base (团队知识库) - `runbook` (operational procedures, kept current — stale runbooks get `status: superseded` with a link to the replacement), `faq` (one question per document), `onboarding` (index linking the reading path). ## Attachments are first-class references A wikilink or embed pointing at a canvas-openable attachment (PDF, Office, image, media) — `[[paper.pdf]]`, `![[figure.png]]` — opens it directly in canvas. Cite the attachment, never a bare path string: the link is what makes it reachable, and it also gives the term registry something to resolve against. The graph view listing attachments as nodes is a side effect, not a goal.
